rows.text: Goad does two things at once: it forces a creature to attack, and it forbids it from attacking you. So the deck's job is to point the entire table's board at each other, sit behind a couple of cheap defensive artifacts, and collect the pieces afterwards. The single most important upgrade is Bothersome Quasit, because a goaded creature that also cannot BLOCK means your opponents are simultaneously forced to attack and unable to defend.

rows.name: Karazikar, the Eye Tyrant
rows.text: every time you attack a player, tap AND goad a creature that player controls. Attacking three opponents taps and goads three creatures, and the goad lasts until your next turn — so they spend their whole turn cycle attacking each other.
Attack with anything, even a 1/1. The trigger is on attacking a PLAYER, not on damage, so a chump attacker still goads their best blocker.

rows.name: Lightning Greaves
rows.text: haste and shroud for a five-drop the whole table wants dead.

rows.name: Blackblade Reforged
rows.text: +1/+1 per land on a legendary creature for three. It turns Karazikar into a real clock while the table fights.

rows.name: Bothersome Quasit
rows.text: goaded creatures your opponents control CANNOT BLOCK, and it goads another creature on every noncreature spell you cast. This is the card that turns goad from an annoyance into a lock.

rows.name: Baeloth Barrityl, Entertainer
rows.text: everything smaller than him is permanently goaded, with no work from you.

rows.name: Disrupt Decorum
rows.text: goad every creature you do not control, all at once.

rows.name: Fast Forward
rows.text: the same, and it costs one less per opponent you attacked this turn — which Karazikar encourages anyway.

rows.name: Kardur, Doomscourge
rows.text: everything of theirs attacks, and it drains them for each creature that dies afterwards.

rows.name: Geode Rager
rows.text: goads a whole player's board on every landfall.

rows.name: Grenzo, Havoc Raiser
rows.text: goads on every connection, or steals a card off their library instead.

rows.name: Coercive Impetus
rows.text: a permanent goad on one creature, with a counter.

rows.name: Bloodthirsty Blade
rows.text: a movable permanent goad — attach it to whatever is most dangerous each turn.

rows.name: Hot Pursuit
rows.text: suspects a creature, so it cannot block at all while the enchantment stays out.
Goad says "a player other than you if able", but the table still has creatures that were never goaded. These cover the gap.

rows.name: Crawlspace
rows.text: no more than two creatures can attack you each combat. Against a goaded board this is close to immunity.

rows.name: Forcefield
rows.text: reduces the one big attacker that does get through to a single point.

rows.name: Deadly Rollick
rows.text: free with your commander out, for the creature that would actually kill you.

rows.name: Deflecting Swat
rows.text: free, and it redirects a removal spell or a trigger.

rows.name: Fire Covenant
rows.text: pay life to spread damage across their board at instant speed — usually during their combat, after blockers.

rows.name: Blasphemous Act
rows.text: on a table full of forced attackers, this is one or two mana and resets everything.

rows.name: Grim Hireling
rows.text: two Treasures on every combat damage step. In a deck attacking three players, that is a lot of mana.

rows.name: Black Market Connections
rows.text: three effects a turn, paid in life.

rows.name: Bitterblossom
rows.text: a free flier every upkeep, which is both a chump blocker and an extra attacker to trigger Karazikar.

rows.name: Loyal Apprentice
rows.text: a hasty Thopter each combat while your commander is out.

rows.name: Life of the Party
rows.text: gets +X for every creature that attacked this turn — after a mass goad, that number is enormous.

rows.name: Jeska's Will
rows.text: with a commander out, both halves: a mana burst and three impulse cards.

rows.name: Kiki-Jiki, Mirror Breaker
rows.text: copies a creature for another attack trigger, another goad, and another Grim Hireling payout.

rows.name: Insurrection
rows.text: take every creature on the board, untapped and hasted. After a turn of goading, most of them are already damaged and their controllers have no blockers. This usually ends the game outright.

rows.name: Karazikar, the Eye Tyrant
rows.text: with Blackblade Reforged attached, he is a fifteen-power trampler while everyone else is busy.

rows.name: Life of the Party
rows.text: the other finisher — one enormous first-striking trampler after a table-wide attack.

rows.name: Grenzo, Havoc Raiser
rows.text: steals the cards you need while chipping in.

rows.name: Chaos Warp
rows.text: Rakdos's answer to an enchantment or planeswalker.

rows.name: Dauthi Voidwalker
rows.text: unblockable, blanks their graveyards, and steals their best card.

rows.name: Boggart Trawler
rows.text: graveyard hate on a body, and a land when you need one.

rows.name: Hexing Squelcher
rows.text: your spells cannot be countered and your creatures get ward.

rows.name: Demonic Tutor
rows.text: any card.

rows.name: Liquimetal Torque
rows.text: fixes, and turns a problem permanent into an artifact for removal.

rows.name: Mind Stone
rows.text: ramp early, a card later.

rows.name: Fellwar Stone
rows.text: usually taps for what you need.

guide.title: What to keep in an opening hand

rows.text: Keep a rock and a defensive artifact. Crawlspace on turn three means the goaded board genuinely cannot reach you, which is what makes the whole plan safe rather than merely chaotic.

Attack every turn, with everything, at every opponent you can. Karazikar's trigger is per player attacked, so spreading one creature each at three players is three goads — far better than sending everything at one person.

rows.name: Bothersome Quasit
rows.text: find it. Goad alone makes them attack; Quasit makes them unable to block, which converts the table's forced attacks into a board wipe they perform on each other.

rows.name: Insurrection
rows.text: hold it until two opponents are low and their boards are still large. Taking a goaded, damaged table's creatures is usually lethal to more than one player at once.
